column5: You know what that means, right?\nAs soon as we get there — I'm buying apples.
column6: 你知道那意味着什么吧？\n我们一到那儿——我就要去买苹果。

column5: Oh — well, I don't blame you.\nThe beds at home are a lot more comfortable.\nI heard Ulric talking outside. We're skipping breakfast.
column6: 哦——好吧，我不怪你。\n家里的床确实舒服多了。\n我听到乌尔里克在外面说话了。我们不吃早饭了。

column5: When we're all ready, we're heading to Mazeo.\nI think you can tell what I'm planning, right?\nWe'll finally be able to share some apples!
column6: 等我们准备好了，就出发去马泽奥。\n我猜你能看出我在打什么主意吧？\n我们终于能一起分享苹果了！

column5: He smiles, and his ears perk up.{w}\nSkipping breakfast didn't sound all too appealing.{w}\nBut I'm sure Mazeo would have no shortage of cuisine.
column6: 他笑了，耳朵竖了起来。{w}\n不吃早饭听起来可不太吸引人。{w}\n不过我敢肯定马泽奥不缺美食。

column5: Someone knocks on the door to the room a few times.{w}\nAfter hearing no objections, they slowly enter the room.{w}\nIt's Valessa, and she lets out a loud yawn before speaking.
column6: 有人敲了几下房门。{w}\n见没人反对，他们缓缓走进房间。{w}\n是瓦莱莎，她打了个大大的哈欠才开口。

column5: Oh, hey Fortaime.\nI was gonna look for you, too.\nGlad to know I didn't end up wasting time.
column6: 哦，嘿，福泰姆。\n我本来也想去找你来着。\n还好我没白跑一趟。

column5: Morning, Valessa. Sleep well?
column6: 早上好，瓦莱莎。睡得好吗？

column5: I suppose so, all things considered.\nThere's a whole host of questions I want to ask.\nAs soon as we meet Damek, I expect to get answers.
column6: 算是吧，考虑到种种情况。\n我有一大堆问题想问。\n一见到达梅克，我希望能得到答案。

column5: Yeah, I know what you mean.\nHopefully as The Elder, I can get him to talk.\nIt's a bit different when it's a political ally asking.
column6: 是啊，我懂你的意思。\n希望以长老的身份，我能让他开口。\n由政治盟友来问，总归不太一样。

column5: Makes sense, I guess.\nMaybe I'll give you my list or something.\nThen it'll be a matter of Mazeo-Valinorth relations.
column6: 我想也有道理。\n也许我该把我的清单交给你之类的。\n那就成了马泽奥和瓦利诺斯之间的外交事务了。

column5: Not a bad idea, actually.\nEither way, I expect to know a lot more in a few days.\nI can't wait to meet Damek and the rest of the Rebel Alliance.
column6: 其实这主意不坏。\n不管怎样，几天后我应该能了解得多得多。\n我迫不及待想见到达梅克和反抗军同盟的其他成员了。

column5: Without hesitation, the door swings open a few moments later.{w}\nValessa and Fortaime enter, displaying a level of energy that makes me envious.{w}\nIt must be time to leave. As soon as we walked out that door, our journey would begin.
column6: 片刻之后，门毫不犹豫地被推开了。{w}\n瓦莱莎和福泰姆走了进来，那股活力让我有些羡慕。{w}\n该出发了。只要走出那扇门，我们的旅程就开始了。

column5: I say nothing, but I know for a fact that this will not dissuade whoever's there.{w}\nThere is hesitance however, and I hear multiple voices coming from the other side.{w}\nEventually, they subside, and soon after, the door to my room opens.
column6: 我什么也没说，但我很清楚这吓不退门外的人。{w}\n不过门外的人犹豫了，我听到好几个声音。{w}\n最后他们安静下来，没过多久，我房间的门就开了。

column5: Hey, [firstname]! Good morning!\nWe all slept in a bit late, so we're skipping breakfast.\nUlric's orders, so there's no point in fighting it, right?
column6: 嘿，[firstname]！早上好！\n我们都睡过头了一点，所以不吃早饭了。\n乌尔里克的命令，反抗也没用，对吧？

column5: Hey, [firstname]! Good morning!\nWe all slept in a bit late, so we're skipping breakfast.\nUlric's orders, so there's no point in fighting it, right?
column6: 嘿，[firstname]！早上好！\n我们都睡过头了一点，所以不吃早饭了。\n乌尔里克的命令，反抗也没用，对吧？

column5: Yeah, but our next stop is Mazeo!\nAs soon as we get there, I'll buy us all apples.\nMan, it's been {i}way{/i} too long since I've had those!
column6: 是啊，但我们的下一站是马泽奥！\n一到那儿，我就给大家买苹果。\n天哪，我{i}真的{/i}太久没吃过那种苹果了！

column5: A one track mind, as usual.\nBut to be honest, it does sound tasty.\nHopefully they aren't too expensive.
column6: 还是老样子，满脑子就一件事。\n不过说实话，听起来确实好吃。\n希望别太贵。

column5: So, are you ready to go?\nUlric and Pro are waiting out front.\nI guess The Outlook is pretty close to Peregrino.
column6: 那么，你准备好出发了吗？\n乌尔里克和普洛在外面等着。\n我想瞭望台离佩雷格里诺挺近的。

column5: I'm good. \nUnless there's something else we need to do?
column6: 我准备好了。\n除非还有别的事要做？

column5: They both look at me. I guess it's my choice.{w}\nIt might be a good chance to get some private time with my friends.{w}\nBut Ulric and Pro could get impatient if we waste time chatting in Peregrino.
column6: 他们俩都看着我。看来决定权在我。{w}\n这也许是个和朋友私下相处的好机会。{w}\n但要是我们在佩雷格里诺闲聊浪费时间，乌尔里克和普洛可能会不耐烦。

column5: Either way, I know {i}one{/i} thing for certain. I shouldn't tell them what happened.{w}\nThe Triumvirate taking me to their chambers, and personally? Would they even believe me?{w}\nI should let it process for a bit longer, and see if it happens again before telling anybody.
column6: 不管怎样，有{i}一件事{/i}我十分确定。我不该告诉他们发生了什么。{w}\n三人执政团亲自把我带到他们的内室？他们会相信我吗？{w}\n我应该再消化一阵子，看看会不会再发生，然后再告诉别人。

column5: I pause, and they await my next move.
column6: 我停顿了一下，他们等着我的下一步。

column5: Sovy looked at the sea, taking in every detail of the near-infinite expanse.{w}\nStill processing the earlier revelations, he gritted his teeth, annoyed.{w}\nWhy did The Triumvirate wait so long to tell him these secrets?
column6: 索维望着大海，将这片近乎无垠的广阔尽收眼底。{w}\n还在消化先前的那些真相，他恼怒地咬紧了牙关。{w}\n三人执政团为什么等了这么久才把这些秘密告诉他？

column5: Master, are you okay?
column6: 师父，您还好吗？

column5: Of course.
column6: 当然。

column5: There it is again — that dismissive tone.\nI can tell when something is wrong, you know.\nThere's no need to lie. I'm your {i}Apprentice{/i}.
column6: 又来了——又是那种敷衍的语气。\n你知道的，有事瞒不过我。\n没必要撒谎。我是您的{i}学徒{/i}。

column5: It's nothing, Halin.
column6: 没什么，哈林。

column5: I think it has to do with what happened earlier.\nThe Triumvirate told you something, didn't they?\nYou're not taking it well. I could tell the entire time.
column6: 我想这和之前发生的事有关。\n三人执政团跟你说了什么，对吧？\n你接受不了。我全程都看得出来。

column5: Very perceptive. Leave me alone.
column6: 挺敏锐的。别烦我。

column5: Sovy, you're acting like a child.
column6: 索维，你表现得像个孩子。

column5: He lets out a deep sigh, as his Apprentice hounds him for information.{w}\nIt was true, but Sovy didn't want to admit it. He was too prideful.
column6: 学徒追问个不停，他深深叹了口气。{w}\n这是事实，可索维不想承认。他太骄傲了。

column5: Please tell me. I want to help you, Sovy.\nI stand by your side, no matter what.
column6: 请告诉我吧。我想帮你，索维。\n无论发生什么，我都站在你这边。

column5: Are you sure about that, Halin?
column6: 你确定吗，哈林？

column5: Of course.\nYou don't have to tell me what they said, Sovy.\nBut at least tell me what you're {i}feeling{/i}.
column6: 当然。\n你不必告诉我他们说了什么，索维。\n但至少告诉我你的{i}感受{/i}。

column5: Sovy took note of Halin's sudden empathy.{w}\nIt was abnormal, and somewhat unwelcome.{w}\nWhat had changed in the last few hours?
column6: 索维注意到哈林突然表现出的共情。{w}\n这很不寻常，甚至有点不受欢迎。{w}\n过去几个小时里，是什么变了？

column5: They told me something I wasn't ready to hear.\nI'm sorry I forgot about you, and I'm sorry for being cross.\nMy thoughts are muddled, Halin — and I'm confused.
column6: 他们告诉了我一些我还没准备好接受的事。\n抱歉我忽略了你，也抱歉我态度不好。\n我的思绪很乱，哈林——我很困惑。

column5: How do you plan to deal with that?
column6: 你打算怎么应对？

column5: For the first time in a while, I don't know.\nMy purpose was always clear — my resolve, unwavering.\nI'm starting to feel like my previous Master, before my promotion.
column6: 这么久以来，我第一次不知道。\n我的信念一向明确——我的决心从未动摇。\n我开始觉得，自己像极了晋升前的那位师父。

column5: You never did tell me what happened to him.
column6: 你从没告诉过我他后来怎么了。

column5: No, I didn't.
column6: 是没有。

column5: Very well.\nAt least tell me about this \"purpose\" of yours.\nI fight to ensure the reign of The Triumvirate — our Gods.
column6: 好吧。\n那至少跟我讲讲你的那个“信念”。\n我战斗，是为了确保三人执政团——我们的神——的统治。

column5: A very clear purpose, and noble to some.\nFor me, things have always been a bit different.\nI fight to ensure the reign of Alestia's true rulers.
column6: 一个非常明确的信念，对某些人来说也很高尚。\n但对我来说，情况一直有些不同。\n我战斗，是为了确保阿莱斯蒂亚真正统治者的统治。

column5: Then what's the issue, Master?\nIt would seem that we share the same purpose.
column6: 那问题出在哪儿，师父？\n看起来我们的信念是一样的。

column5: Sovy sighed again, and slumped his shoulders slightly.{w}\nUntil now, everything had been an act to intimidate Shane.{w}\nHalin could tell that Sovy was displaying his true emotions.
column6: 索维又叹了口气，肩膀微微垮了下来。{w}\n在此之前，他所做的一切都是为了震慑肖恩而演的戏。{w}\n哈林看得出来，索维流露的是真实情绪。

column5: Normally, I would agree with you.\nBut now...? Now, I'm not so sure.
column6: 通常我会同意你。\n但现在……？现在，我不太确定了。

column5: No Alex, you have it all wrong.\nI only want you to {i}pretend{/i} that you're helping The Triumvirate.\nWhen the time comes, you'll turn on them and help Damek instead.
column6: 不，亚历克斯，你全搞错了。\n我只是要你{i}假装{/i}在帮三人执政团。\n时候一到，你就反戈一击，转而帮达梅克。

column5: You know Nada will never let this happen, right?
column6: 你知道娜达绝不会让这种事发生的，对吧？

column5: I don't care what she thinks. I'm asking {i}you{/i}.\nI have no doubt in my mind — a battle is coming to Mazeo.\nThe Triumvirate will send their forces here for that new idol.
column6: 我不在乎她怎么想。我在问你{i}本人{/i}。\n我毫不怀疑——一场战斗即将降临马泽奥。\n三人执政团会为了那尊新的灵像派兵过来。

column5: I don't know what they want with it, but we need to strike immediately.\nYou'll meet them at the docks, and tell them you've been hired to assist.\nAs soon as you get the chance, you'll sabotage the ships, and kill them all.
column6: 我不知道他们要那东西做什么，但我们必须立刻动手。\n你去码头接应他们，就说你是被雇来帮忙的。\n一有机会，你就破坏船只，把他们全部杀掉。

column5: That is, except for {i}one{/i} ship.\nDamek will need one to launch his attack on Balteus.
column6: 当然，除了{i}一艘{/i}船。\n达梅克需要一艘船来对巴尔泰乌斯发动进攻。

column5: Alright, I'll humor you for a moment.\nEven if I play along, and your Rebellion comes to rule Alestia?\nThey'll lift the trade bans, effectively ruining piracy for good.
column6: 好吧，我就陪你玩一会儿。\n就算我配合你，你们的反抗军真的统治了阿莱斯蒂亚？\n他们会解除贸易禁令，那等于彻底毁掉海盗这一行。

column5: Why should I fight to kill my own profession?
column6: 我为什么要拼命去毁掉自己的营生？

column5: There are much better things to do in this world, Alex.\nI could pay you with anything you wanted — or any job you wanted.\nJust name it, and I'll make it happen. These are dire times, you know.
column6: 这世上比这更好的事多的是，亚历克斯。\n你要什么报酬都行——想要什么差事也行。\n尽管开口，我来办。你知道的，眼下是非常时期。

column5: I doubt this offer extends to the rest of our crew.\nI'd love a reward, and a new job, but not if it screws them over.\nThey'll be doing the bulk of the fighting. Not me, or Nada.
column6: 我怀疑这条件不会惠及我们其他船员。\n报酬和新差事我乐意要，但不能害了他们。\n打仗的主力是他们。不是我，也不是娜达。

column5: That is, if I can even convince them to do this.\nOne of our core tenets is that we don't take sides.
column6: 前提还是我能不能说服他们干这事。\n我们不选边站，这是我们的核心信条之一。

column5: Even when the victor is clear?
column6: 就算胜者已定？

column5: Even so.\nDuring the occupation, we fought for our own survival.\nBoth The Triumvirate {i}and{/i} the citizens of Mazeo attacked us.
column6: 即便如此。\n占领期间，我们为自己的生存而战。\n三人执政团{i}和{/i}马泽奥的市民都袭击过我们。

column5: We worked for decades to unite the pirates into what they are today.\nDoing this will split them apart again. You'll make an enemy out of Nada.\nShe's pretty much the leader, and her influence is immeasurable.
column6: 我们花了几十年才把海盗们团结成今天这个样子。\n这么做会让他们再次分裂。你会和娜达为敌。\n她基本上就是首领，影响力不可估量。

column5: I'm well aware of that, and I've taken it into consideration.\nA divide in your numbers will still give me the right amount of men.\nYou can show the rest of the pirates they're on the wrong side of this.
column6: 我很清楚，也已经考虑过了。\n你们的人就算分裂，留给我的兵力也刚刚好。\n你可以让其余的海盗看看，他们站错了边。

column5: Any divide that comes, I'm sure we can mend it.\nBesides, Damek hasn't {i}said{/i} he's going to harm piracy.\nI'm sure we can come to some sort of deal, Alex.
column6: 就算出现分裂，我相信我们也能弥合。\n再说，达梅克并没{i}说过{/i}他要打击海盗。\n我相信我们能谈成某种交易，亚历克斯。

column5: No matter what the deal is, you can't win over {i}everybody{/i}.\nAs soon as The Triumvirate falls, you'll have another war lined up.\nHell — they might even join the white-cloaks out of spite.
column6: 不管是什么交易，你都不可能收服{i}所有人{/i}。\n三人执政团一倒，下一场战争就排上日程了。\n见鬼——他们甚至可能出于怨气加入白袍军。

column5: I'm willing to take the risk.\nBut I'll do my best to make sure they're satisfied.\nThere will be a place for {i}everyone{/i} in our new Alestia.
column6: 我愿意冒这个险。\n但我会尽力让他们满意。\n在我们新的阿莱斯蒂亚里，会{i}人人{/i}都有位置。

column5: The pirates are in a great position to make demands.\nAs the Mayor of Mazeo, I can give you anything you want.\nThere's no way Nada could turn an offer like that down.
column6: 海盗们正处在提条件的好位置。\n作为马泽奥的市长，你要什么我都能给。\n娜达不可能拒绝这样的条件。

column5: Very well. Let's talk terms.
column6: 很好。我们来谈条件吧。

column5: Damek ventured back underground from the Church of Mazeo.{w}\nAfter a lengthy journey through the tunnels — he was home.{w}\nThe deed was secured, and they had everything they needed.
column6: 达梅克从马泽奥教堂再次潜入地下。{w}\n在隧道里走了漫长的路——他到家了。{w}\n地契到手了，他们需要的一切都齐了。

column5: Why did the Honor Guard do all of this...?\nThey single-handedly sheltered and armed our forces.
column6: 荣誉卫队为什么做了这一切……？\n他们单凭一己之力就为我们的部队提供了庇护和武器。

column5: One of the rebels notices Damek's sudden entrance.{w}\nHe quickly stands up, and greets the General with a smile.
column6: 一个反抗军成员注意到达梅克突然进来。{w}\n他迅速站起身，笑着迎接将军。

column5: Damek, Sir!\nEverything is going according to plan.\nOur forces have started to relocate.
column6: 达梅克，长官！\n一切都按计划进行。\n我们的部队已经开始转移。

column5: Perfect timing, Vance.\nI just received the deed from Gryz.\nIt took some convincing, but I did it.
column6: 来得正好，万斯。\n我刚从格瑞兹那里拿到地契。\n费了些口舌，不过办成了。

column5: Wait — you didn't already have the deed?\nWhy were we moving everybody down here...?
column6: 等等——你之前还没拿到地契？\n那我们为什么把所有人都转移到这儿来……？

column5: Oops. You didn't hear anything, alright?\nBesides, I knew I could win him over.\nThis was just a bit of a... \"head start\".
column6: 哎呀。你什么都没听见，好吗？\n再说，我知道我能说服他。\n这不过是……“抢先一步”罢了。

column5: And cut the formalities — call me Damek.\nWe've been through enough. This isn't about rank.\nI think of us all as a family, not an army.
column6: 还有，别搞那些客套——叫我达梅克。\n我们一起经历得够多了。这不是讲军衔的时候。\n我把我们所有人都当家人，而不是军队。

column5: Of course, Damek.\nI'm amazed at our new HQ, to be honest.\nHow did you secure all of this stuff...?
column6: 当然，达梅克。\n说实话，我对我们的新总部感到惊叹。\n你是怎么弄到这些东西的……？

column5: It wasn't me, Vance.\nThe Honor Guard was planning a {i}long{/i} stay.\nThey're responsible for everything you see.
column6: 不是我弄的，万斯。\n荣誉卫队本来是打算{i}长期{/i}驻留的。\n你看到的一切都是他们置办的。

column5: You mean those {i}things{/i}?\nWhy would they build stuff they have no use for?\nThey can't really fight, and they have no need for sleep.
column6: 你是说那些{i}东西{/i}？\n他们为什么会建造自己用不上的东西？\n他们根本没法打仗，也不需要睡觉。

column5: Damek smirked and grabbed a blade from the nearby shelf.
column6: 达梅克笑了笑，从旁边的架子上抓起一把剑。

column5: They must've known {i}someone{/i} would use it.\nEither way — The Triumvirate doesn't know about this.\nTheir own Honor Guard is defying orders, it would seem.
column6: 他们一定知道{i}有人{/i}会用得上。\n不管怎样——三人执政团并不知道这事。\n看来他们自己的荣誉卫队在违抗命令。

column5: Vance followed Damek's lead, and grabbed a blade as well.
column6: 万斯学着达梅克的样子，也抓起一把剑。

column5: So there's discord among them...?\nNever thought we'd live to see that.
column6: 这么说他们内部也有矛盾……？\n从没想过我们这辈子能见到这种事。

column5: Yeah, but it also proves The Triumvirate isn't all-knowing.\nThere's no way they'd let this happen if they were.\nThey're just like us. We can take them down.
column6: 是啊，但这也证明三人执政团并非无所不知。\n要是他们真全知全能，绝不会让这种事发生。\n他们和我们一样。我们能打倒他们。

column5: He flourishes his blade, and holds it out.
column6: 他耍了个剑花，把剑横举起来。

column5: That is — if we're strong enough.
column6: 前提是——我们足够强。

column5: It's a spar you want...?
column6: 你是想切磋一下……？

column5: Vance smirks and mimics the flourish of his General.{w}\nA few of the nearby rebels stop in their tracks to watch.
column6: 万斯咧嘴一笑，模仿起将军的剑花。{w}\n附近几个反抗军成员停下脚步围观。

column5: Just need to make sure you haven't gotten sloppy.\nAs soon as The Triumvirate finds out — a fight is coming.
column6: 只是得确认你没生疏。\n三人执政团一旦发现——一场战斗就要来了。

column5: Don't worry Damek. I'm ready.
column6: 别担心，达梅克。我准备好了。

column5: They charge at each other, and their swords clash.{w}\nThe loud clang of steel against steel fills their HQ.{w}\nAs the audience grows in size, their morale rises in tandem.
column6: 两人冲向对方，剑刃相交。{w}\n钢铁相击的巨响回荡在整个总部。{w}\n围观的人越来越多，他们的士气也随之高涨。

column5: After a trek that was longer than expected, we finally reach The Outlook.{w}\nThere was a long uphill walk, so my legs are strained and tired.{w}\nThat, along with my lack of sleep, was an unfortunate combination.
column6: 走了比预想更远的路，我们终于到了瞭望台。{w}\n一路长长的上坡，我的腿又酸又累。{w}\n再加上睡眠不足，真是糟糕的组合。

column5: Well, here we are.\nZamira told me you've never been.\nTake a look down there. What do you think?
column6: 好了，我们到了。\n扎米拉跟我说过你没来过这儿。\n往下看看吧。觉得怎么样？

column5: He lets out a soft laugh, like he's anticipating our reaction.{w}\nAfter a few more steps, we reach the high ground, and everything comes into view.{w}\nThe scope of our world, and just how small Valinorth really was, finally dawned upon me.
column6: 他轻轻笑了一声，仿佛在期待我们的反应。{w}\n又走了几步，我们来到高处，眼前豁然开朗。{w}\n我终于意识到我们的世界有多辽阔，而瓦利诺斯又有多渺小。

column5: Whoa...
That's amazing!
column6: 太惊人了！

column5: They stop to catch their breath, as they run up the hill in excitement.{w}\nWe can see the entirety of Mazeo, and it looks so tiny from up here.{w}\nBut I know it's {i}much{/i} larger than Valinorth, so this is hard to comprehend.
column6: 他们兴奋地跑上山坡，停下来喘口气。{w}\n整个马泽奥尽收眼底，从这里看过去小得可怜。{w}\n但我知道它比瓦利诺斯{i}大得多{/i}，所以这实在让人难以置信。

column5: That's Mazeo...?
column6: 那就是马泽奥……？

column5: Yeah. We can probably reach it in a few more hours.\nBut take a while to enjoy the view — it's really something else.\nAnd it's not like we'll be coming back here anytime soon, right?
column6: 是啊。再走几个小时应该就能到了。\n不过多花点时间欣赏风景吧——真的很不一般。\n反正我们短期内也不会再回来了，对吧？

column5: Yeah...
column6: 是啊……

column5: Pro takes a few steps forward, writing in some kind of journal.{w}\nHe watches Ulric, not even needing to stare at the paper as he wrote.
column6: 普洛上前几步，在本子上写着什么。{w}\n他望着乌尔里克，写字时甚至不用看纸。

column5: And so, Ulric stood at the entrance of the world, enthralled by its beauty.\nIt would seem that his dreams for the future were no less grand than the sight before him.\nWith comrades in tow, they took in the sight together, an unspoken bond slowly forming.
column6: 就这样，乌尔里克站在世界的入口，被它的美景深深吸引。\n看来他对未来的梦想，丝毫不逊于眼前的景象。\n与同伴们同行，他们一同凝望着这片景色，一种无言的羁绊正悄然形成。

column5: The bond won't last much longer if you keep that up, Pro.
column6: 你再这样下去，这羁绊可维持不了多久，普洛。

column5: Yikes.\nIt's not like this is my job or anything.\nYou know I'm trying to record all the important moments.
column6: 哎呀。\n又不是说这是我的分内工作。\n你知道的，我只是想记录下所有重要时刻。

column5: You must be grasping at straws if you're writing about me, then.\nFocus on the Seer or something. This is the start of his journey.
column6: 那你要写我，可真是没素材可写了。\n写写先知什么的吧。这是他的旅程的起点。

column5: You must be grasping at straws if you're writing about me, then.\nFocus on the Seeress or something. This is the start of her journey.
column6: 那你要写我，可真是没素材可写了。\n写写先知什么的吧。这是她的旅程的起点。

column5: Or — maybe you could focus on this...?
column6: 或者——也许你可以写写这个……？

column5: Huh...?

We all turn to Fortaime, and he's holding out his hands.{w}\nInside of the cup he's formed with them, rests a single crimson leaf.{w}\nA breeze flows through the area, sending a chill through all of us.
column6: 我们都转向福泰姆，他伸出双手。{w}\n在他双手窝成的杯状里，静静躺着一片深红的叶子。{w}\n一阵微风拂过，让我们所有人都打了个寒战。

column5: Immediately, we turn toward Valinorth, in awe of what we see.{w}\nThe bloodleaves are falling, making their journey through the sky.{w}\nCarried by the chilling wind, they find their way down to the mainland.
column6: 我们立刻转向瓦利诺斯，被眼前的景象震撼。{w}\n血叶正在飘落，踏上穿越天空的旅途。{w}\n它们被凛冽的风托着，一路飘向大陆。

column5: Wow...
This shouldn't be happening, right...?\nThe bloodleaves don't fall at this time of year!
column6: 这不正常吧……？\n这个时节血叶不该落的！

column5: He's right, everyone.\nNormally it's too warm for them to wilt and fall.\nI know what this means. Valinorth is... starting to die...
column6: 大家，他说得对。\n通常天太暖和，它们不会枯萎掉落。\n我知道这意味着什么。瓦利诺斯……开始走向衰亡了……

column5: You mean because of the dimmed spirit idol?
column6: 你是说因为那尊黯淡的灵像？

column5: Yeah. I didn't think it would happen so fast.\nWe need to hurry. If we don't do something, our home will—
column6: 嗯。我没想到会来得这么快。\n我们得抓紧了。如果再不做点什么，我们的家园就要——

column5: Ulric steps forward, and rests a hand on Valessa's shoulder.
column6: 乌尔里克上前一步，把手搭在瓦莱莎的肩上。

column5: Don't worry. \nWe'll figure out a way to save your village.\nWe're saving Alestia — and that includes Valinorth.
column6: 别担心。\n我们会找到办法救你们的村子。\n我们是在拯救阿莱斯蒂亚——瓦利诺斯也包括在内。

column5: She nods, and we turn back to stare down at the mainland.{w}\nFor a moment, the falling of the bloodleaves was a more beautiful sight.{w}\nBut was this a blessing, or perhaps a portend of bad things to come...?
column6: 她点点头，我们重新望向下方的大陆。{w}\n有那么一瞬间，飘落的血叶显得更美了。{w}\n可这是福兆，还是厄运将至的预兆……？

column5: Pro remains silent, but continues writing in his notebook.{w}\nSurely this would give him enough material to keep busy for a while.{w}\nI look at Valessa and Fortaime, and they give me nervous smiles.
column6: 普洛沉默不语，继续在本子上记录。{w}\n这下总够他忙活一阵子了。{w}\n我看向瓦莱莎和福泰姆，他们冲我露出不安的笑容。

column5: Are you ready, [firstname]...?\nI guess this is where things truly begin.
column6: 你准备好了吗，[firstname]……？\n我想，一切真正开始的地方，就是这里了。

column5: Are you ready, [firstname]...?\nI guess this is where things truly begin.
column6: 你准备好了吗，[firstname]……？\n我想，一切真正开始的地方，就是这里了。

column5: As a team — we can do this.\nI'm stronger for having you by my side.
column6: 作为一个团队——我们做得到。\n有你在身边，我变得更强了。

column5: Ulric takes a few steps back, letting us have our moment.{w}\nHe knew how important this was to the three of us.{w}\nIt was perhaps the biggest moment of our lives.
column6: 乌尔里克后退了几步，把这一刻留给我们。{w}\n他知道这对我们三个人有多重要。{w}\n这也许是我们一生中最重要的时刻。

column5: So this is it, huh...?
column6: 那么就是现在了，嗯……？

column5: She lets go of the bloodleaves she held in her hand.{w}\nThe gust of wind from behind us helps them sail down to Mazeo.
column6: 她松开手里的血叶。{w}\n身后吹来的一阵风托着它们飘向马泽奥。

column5: Now it's our turn...
column6: 轮到我们了……

column5: I notice Fortaime wipe his eyes with his forearm. Was he crying...?{w}\nIt's probably best not to point it out, as I don't want to embarrass him.{w}\nHe clenches his fists, and looks to the sky with closed eyes.
column6: 我注意到福泰姆用前臂擦了擦眼睛。他哭了吗……？{w}\n最好还是别提，我不想让他难堪。{w}\n他攥紧拳头，闭着眼仰望天空。

column5: I wish you could be here with us.\nDon't worry, Mom and Dad. I'll make you proud...
column6: 真希望你们能和我们在一起。\n别担心，爸、妈。我会让你们骄傲的……

column5: He turns to us and smiles. Ulric can tell that the moment is over.{w}\nWithout saying anything, he starts walking down The Outlook.{w}\nFrom what I can see, a trail takes us all the way to Mazeo.
column6: 他转向我们，笑了笑。乌尔里克看得出，这一刻结束了。{w}\n他什么也没说，开始沿着瞭望台往下走。{w}\n我看得出来，有一条小路一直通向马泽奥。

column5: This is it. This was the moment our journey began.
column6: 就是现在。我们的旅程，就是从这一刻开始的。

column5: The Triumvirate gathered in their chambers, near the glowing idol.{w}\nWith a faint smile on their faces, they gazed deep into its corruption.{w}\nAs nobody else was in sight, they had no need to keep up appearances.
column6: 三人执政团聚在内室里，靠近那尊发光的灵像。{w}\n他们脸上带着淡淡的笑意，凝视着它深处的腐化。{w}\n四下无人，他们不必再装模作样。

column5: It appears that things have finally begun.\nDid you have your audience with The Seer, Master?
column6: 看来一切终于开始了。\n师父，您和先知会过面了吗？

column5: It appears that things have finally begun.\nDid you have your audience with The Seeress, Master?
column6: 看来一切终于开始了。\n师父，您和先知会过面了吗？

column5: Yes, indeed.\nIt went just as planned.\nDoubt is a very powerful weapon.
column6: 是的，没错。\n一切都在计划之中。\n怀疑是非常强大的武器。

column5: When wielded properly, you are right.\nThankfully, we have lots of practice.
column6: 用得恰当的话，你说得没错。\n好在，我们练习得够多了。

column5: Perhaps too much...?
column6: 也许练得太多了……？

column5: Or at the very least, not enough.\nBut we've waited longer in the past.
column6: 又或者，至少还不够多。\n不过过去我们等得更久。

column5: One of The Triumvir's lowers their hood.{w}\nTaking a deep breath, they sigh in relief.
column6: 三人执政团中的一人放下兜帽。{w}\n他深吸一口气，如释重负地叹了出来。

column5: So you think this is the end...?
column6: 所以你觉得这就是终局了……？

column5: The other Triumvir follows in turn, lowering his hood.{w}\nHowever, their master chooses not to do the same.
column6: 另一位执政官也跟着放下兜帽。{w}\n然而，他们的师父却选择不这么做。

column5: I suppose that rests with The Seer.\nLet us watch, and see what unfolds.
column6: 我想这取决于先知。\n我们就看着吧，看事情如何发展。

column5: I suppose that rests with The Seeress.\nLet us watch, and see what unfolds.
column6: 我想这取决于先知。\n我们就看着吧，看事情如何发展。

column5: Wow, I didn't expect you to dress {i}that{/i} fancy!\nI'm a little jealous now, I feel underdressed.\nYou should do my wardrobe next time we go out!
column6: 哇，没想到你穿得{i}那么{/i}讲究！\n我现在有点嫉妒了，感觉自己穿得太随便。\n下次我们出门，你来给我搭配衣服吧！

column5: Wow, I didn't expect you to look {i}that{/i} fancy!\nNice dress, you're really pulling it off.\nYou should do my wardrobe next time we go out!
column6: 哇，没想到你打扮得{i}那么{/i}讲究！\n裙子真好看，你很撑得起。\n下次我们出门，你来给我搭配衣服吧！

column5: Hey, are you okay?\nYou look a little shaken up.\nAre you nervous about the ceremony?
column6: 嘿，你还好吗？\n你看起来有点心神不宁。\n是在为仪式紧张吗？

column5: Oh, I see...\nPerhaps we should find Valessa first.\nIt must've been bad if you're acting like this.
column6: 哦，我明白了……\n也许我们该先找到瓦莱莎。\n你都这样了，事情肯定不轻。

column5: But hold on, just remember the basics.
column6: 不过等等，记住最基本的几点。

column5: Visions are never foolproof, they're always full of errors.\nIt's like looking at a painting, it's up to interpretation.\nEveryone who looks at it would walk away with something different.
column6: 幻象从来都不是万无一失的，总是充满谬误。\n就像看一幅画，全凭各人解读。\n每个人看完，得到的都不一样。

column5: Not that I have visions, I'm just trying to help.\nValessa will make sense of everything you saw, I know it.\nSometimes visions make mountains out of mudpiles.
column6: 倒不是说我有幻象，我只是想帮忙。\n瓦莱莎一定能理清你看到的一切，我敢肯定。\n有时候幻象会把泥堆看成大山。

column5: Whoa, really!?\nScare me half to death, why don't you.\nLet's put everything on hold then, and get Valessa.
column6: 哇，真的假的！？\n你想把我吓个半死是吧。\n那我们把一切先放一放，去找瓦莱莎。

column5: We're supposed to meet her in the Town Square, [firstname].\nBut if this is as bad as you say, you better tell me, too.\nNot as a Scribe-in-training, but as a friend, got it...?
column6: 我们本该在中央广场跟她碰面，[firstname]。\n但要是真像你说的那么严重，你也得告诉我。\n不是以见习书记官的身份，而是以朋友的身份，明白吗……？

column5: Hey, you really need to stop saying weird stuff.\nYou're gonna make me blush in front of everyone else!
column6: 嘿，你真的别再讲那些奇怪的话了。\n你要让我在大家面前脸红了！

column5: Whoa, I'm not asking you to break the rules...!\nActually, I guess I am, if you really wanna label it.\nBut that makes me sound like such a bad person!
column6: 哇，我不是要你去违反规矩……！\n其实吧，你要真想这么说，那也算。\n可这样显得我像个大坏蛋！

column5: Whoa, I'm not asking you to break anything...!\nActually, I guess I am, if you really wanna label it.\nBut that makes me sound like such a bad person!
column6: 哇，我不是要你去打破什么……！\n其实吧，你要真想这么说，那也算。\n可这样显得我像个大坏蛋！

column5: Alright, I know how it is, and I understand.\nI know you wouldn't purposely put me in any danger.\nSo whatever you end up doing, it's for the best, right?
column6: 好吧，我懂是怎么回事，也能理解。\n我知道你不会故意让我陷入危险。\n所以不管最后怎么做，都是最好的选择，对吧？

column5: Sweet, glad to know you're on my side...!\nIt's good to have a friend in someone like you.
column6: 太好了，很高兴知道你站在我这边……！\n能和你这样的人做朋友真好。

column5: Anyway, we should head to the Town Square.\nWith this vision business, we'll have a busy day.\nDon't waste too much time, alright?
column6: 总之，我们该去中央广场了。\n出了幻象这档子事，今天有得忙了。\n别浪费太多时间，好吗？

column5: This is my home. There's not much more to say.{w}\nI know it's a mess inside, but I'll have to fix that later.{w}\nMaybe Fortaime and I could have a private word inside.
column6: 这是我家。没什么好多说的。{w}\n我知道里面乱糟糟的，但只能以后再收拾了。{w}\n也许我和福泰姆可以进去私下聊两句。

column5: A bit bigger than my house, but mine has more rooms.\nWhich is better though, more rooms or more space?\nMy interior design books don't really cover that aspect.
column6: 比我家大一点，不过我家房间更多。\n到底哪个更好呢，房间多还是空间大？\n我的室内设计书里还真没讲过这方面。

column5: So, you think more space is better?\nI guess you'll just have to invite me over more often.\nAnd if you ever change your mind, you're welcome at my place.
column6: 这么说，你觉得空间大更好？\n那你就得多请我来做客了。\n要是你哪天改变主意，也欢迎来我那儿。

column5: Oh, so it's privacy you want?\nThere's plenty of that back at my place.\nWhenever you need it, I'm just down the street.
column6: 哦，所以你是想要清静？\n我那儿清静得很。\n什么时候需要，我就在街对面。

column5: The master has spoken.\nI guess it's true though. Work with what you have.\nAnd if you don't have it, someone else surely will!
column6: 大师发话了。\n不过还真有道理。有什么就用什么。\n要是你没有，别人肯定有！

column5: Hey Fortaime, remember those apples you used to love?
column6: 嘿，福泰姆，还记得你以前最爱吃的那种苹果吗？

column5: Yeah, how could I forget?\nYou can't get them anymore, though.\nThe Triumvirate put a trading ban on Mazeo.
column6: 记得，我怎么会忘？\n不过现在吃不到了。\n三人执政团对马泽奥下了贸易禁令。

column5: Remember that time I tricked you...?\nI painted a bunch of rocks red, and put them in a basket.\nI told you the trading ban was lifted. You were ecstatic.
column6: 还记得我那次捉弄你吗……？\n我把一堆石头涂成红色，装进篮子里。\n我骗你说贸易禁令解除了。你高兴坏了。

column5: Yeah, and that was really mean!\nMy parents used to give them to me before, you know...\nThat made me cry more than you'd think.
column6: 记得，那真的很过分！\n你知道，以前我爸妈常给我买那种苹果……\n那次我哭得比你想的要厉害。

column5: Yeah, and I just wanted to apologize.\nThis whole ordeal has me thinking about the past.\nI wish I spent my time in Valinorth a bit better.
column6: 嗯，我只是想道个歉。\n这一连串的遭遇让我总想起过去。\n真希望在瓦利诺斯的那些日子，我能过得更充实些。

column5: Oh, well, I accept your apology.\nBetter late than never, right...?
column6: 哦，好吧，我接受你的道歉。\n迟到总比不到好，对吧……？

column5: Yeah, of course.\nOnce we get to Mazeo, I'll buy you some for real.\nAn apology is lame, I'm gonna make up for what I did.
column6: 嗯，当然。\n等我们到了马泽奥，我真给你买。\n光道歉太敷衍了，我要补偿我做过的。

column5: Aww, are you thinking about me?\nI saw the way you looked at me just now.\nGive it to me straight, what's going on?
column6: 哎呀，你在想我吗？\n我看到你刚刚看我的眼神了。\n老实说吧，怎么回事？

column5: I'll take that as a compliment, actually.\nThe louder you are, the more fun you're having!\nYou'll have to come and join me sometime.
column6: 其实我就当那是夸奖了。\n你越吵，说明你玩得越开心！\n哪天你得来跟我一起玩。

column5: I guess you could say that, yeah.\nBeing a Scribe-in-training is pretty hard work.\nIt's fun to unwind after everything is said and done.
column6: 这么说也行吧，没错。\n当见习书记官可辛苦了。\n等一切忙完再放松一下，挺爽的。

column5: He laughs and turns away from me.{w}\nThere's a hint of a blush on his face, but he covers it up.{w}\nHe's quite reckless in his youth, but isn't almost everyone?
column6: 他笑着从我身边转开。{w}\n他脸上隐约泛红，却掩饰了过去。{w}\n他年纪轻轻，行事莽撞，可谁又不是呢？

column5: I often see Fortaime up here, just passing the time.{w}\nClimbing the trees of Valinorth is his number one hobby.{w}\nHe always talks about how he'll climb The Grand Tree one day.
column6: 我常在这儿看到福泰姆，只是打发时间。{w}\n爬瓦利诺斯的树是他最大的爱好。{w}\n他总说，总有一天要去爬巨树。

column5: There's a village-wide notice posted about your induction.\nI think you'll have quite the audience later tonight, [firstname].\nThere's a big party planned afterwards, too. Dancing and all!
column6: 全村的公告栏上贴了你授职的消息。\n我想今晚你会有一大群观众，[firstname]。\n之后还安排了一场盛大的派对。还有跳舞之类的！

column5: There's a village-wide notice posted about your induction.\nI think you'll have quite the audience later tonight, [firstname].\nThere's a big party planned afterwards, too. Dancing and all!
column6: 全村的公告栏上贴了你授职的消息。\n我想今晚你会有一大群观众，[firstname]。\n之后还安排了一场盛大的派对。还有跳舞之类的！

column5: Sounds like you just don't know how to dance!\nI've been practicing my whole life, I'll have to teach you!\nI'm actually performing the ceremonial dance tonight.
column6: 听起来你就是不会跳舞！\n我练了一辈子，得好好教教你！\n今晚的仪式之舞，其实就是我来跳。

column5: Each time a new Seer or Seeress is inducted, there's a ritual.\nA dance that's supposed to bless our people, and your skill.\nIt's very slow and intricate, I hope to do my best...!
column6: 每有一位新先知授职，都会举行一场仪式。\n一支用来祝福村民、也祝福你能力的舞。\n舞步缓慢又繁复，我希望能做到最好……！

column5: You bet! It's supposed to be the party of a lifetime!\nQuite literally, as there's only one Seer or Seeress per generation.\nIf I were you, I wouldn't make any important plans tomorrow.
column6: 那当然！这可是号称一生只有一次的派对！\n名副其实，因为每一代只有一位先知。\n要是我，明天绝不会安排任何重要的事。

column5: Whoa, you really have to think that one through!\nThis is the most important day of your life. \nAre you sure you want to do that with {i}me{/i}?
column6: 哇，这可真得好好想清楚！\n这是你一生中最重要的日子。\n你确定要跟{i}我{/i}一起吗？

column5: If you're certain, then I'd love to!\nMaybe I'll even give you a refresher course.\nI'm assuming you don't get to do much dancing.
column6: 你要是确定，那我乐意之至！\n说不定我还能给你补补课。\n我猜你平时没什么机会跳舞吧。

column5: Sounds good, just let me know!\nI think your induction will be something special.\nYou should spend it with someone special, as well.
column6: 听起来不错，告诉我一声就行！\n我觉得你的授职仪式会很不寻常。\n你也该和一个特别的人一起度过。

column5: Isn't that cool to think about, [firstname]...?\nThe spirits are artists, and your mind is the canvas.\nThere's so much work required in interpreting visions.
column6: 想想是不是很酷，[firstname]……？\n灵体是艺术家，你的心智就是画布。\n解读幻象可真要下不少功夫。

column5: Isn't that cool to think about, [firstname]...?\nThe spirits are artists, and your mind is the canvas.\nThere's so much work required in interpreting visions.
column6: 想想是不是很酷，[firstname]……？\n灵体是艺术家，你的心智就是画布。\n解读幻象可真要下不少功夫。

column5: Of course, the spirits grow stronger every day.\nIt's already gotten to a point where a Scribe is near useless.\nI have more volumes written on this subject, I'm sure you'll find them.
column6: 当然，灵体每天都在变强。\n已经到了书记官几乎派不上用场的地步。\n关于这方面我写了更多卷册，你一定能找到。

column5: Can you believe how much stronger they've gotten, though?\nI wrote this book years ago, and it's almost outdated.\nWe've been able to witness so much growth in one generation.
column6: 可你能相信它们变强了多少吗？\n这本书是我几年前写的，如今几乎过时了。\n我们竟能在同一代人里见证这么大的变化。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Yeah, of course I do!\nIt's so peaceful, and everyone is so nice.\nI don't think Valinorth has any real downsides.
column6: 嗯，当然喜欢！\n这里这么安宁，大家又都这么友善。\n我觉得瓦利诺斯没什么真正的缺点。

column5: We're not plagued with piracy like Mazeo.\nOur hierarchy works, and we're always stable.\nIf I ever got the chance to leave, I doubt I would.
column6: 我们不像马泽奥那样被海盗问题困扰。\n我们的等级制度运转良好，一直很稳定。\n就算有机会离开，我想我也不会走。

column5: That's partly why I've never left the village.\nI know that Peregrino is out there, and Sauleberg.\nBut I've only heard stories. I've never actually been.
column6: 这也是我一直没离开过村子的部分原因。\n我知道外面有佩雷格里诺，还有索尔伯格。\n但我只听过传闻。从没真正去过。

column5: It's a watering hole, like a bar.\nIt's popular for people on their way to Valinorth.\nThat's why it's called \"The Pilgrim's Tavern\".
column6: 那是个酒馆，像酒吧一样的地方。\n前往瓦利诺斯的人常在那儿落脚。\n所以它叫“朝圣者酒馆”。

column5: It's a good business idea, in my opinion.\nThe road to and from Valinorth is long and arduous.\nI bet everybody wants to stop and grab a drink.
column6: 在我看来，这是个不错的生意点子。\n往返瓦利诺斯的路又长又难走。\n我敢打赌，谁都想停下来喝一杯。

column5: At least, that's what I've heard.\nWe don't get too many outsiders, but it's still in business.\nIt makes me wonder if there's something more to that place.
column6: 至少，我是这么听说的。\n我们这儿来不了多少外人，可它还在营业。\n这让我不禁好奇，那地方是不是另有玄机。

column5: Apparently, each nation has a spirit idol.\nIt's where the spirit realm reaches out into the physical world.\nSauleberg is home to ours, but it's been closed off for a while.
column6: 据说，每个国家都有一尊灵像。\n那是灵界延伸到现实世界的地方。\n我们这尊就供在索尔伯格，不过已经封闭有一阵子了。

column5: It happened around the time we were born, actually.\nSo I've never actually seen one in person.\nJust in drawings that Fortaime and I can find.
column6: 其实，那差不多发生在我们出生的时候。\n所以我从没亲眼见过灵像。\n只在福泰姆和我能找到的图画里见过。

column5: You know how nature is supposed to hold spiritual energy?\nWell, that energy has to come from somewhere, right?\nThe idol is actually what delivers it to the land.
column6: 你知道大自然本该承载着灵力吧？\n那这股能量总得有个来源，对吧？\n其实就是灵像把能量输送到大地的。

column5: But one idol can't cover all of Alestia.\nSo like I said, each nation is supposed to have their own.\nThey're like national treasures, to be heavily guarded.
column6: 但一尊灵像覆盖不了整个阿莱斯蒂亚。\n所以就像我说的，每个国家都该有自己的一尊。\n它们就像国宝，必须严加看守。

column5: I'm not holding my breath, to be honest.\nWe're rather self-sustaining here in Valinorth.\nAs long as we have Seers and Scribes, we'll be good.
column6: 说实话，我不抱什么期望。\n瓦利诺斯挺自给自足的。\n只要我们有先知和书记官，就没问题。

column5: Everything pertaining to our livelihood can be foreseen.\nSo far, we haven't had to forge any alliances or treaties.\nAnd remember, it's been this way for thousands of years.
column6: 一切与我们生计相关的事都能被预见。\n到目前为止，我们从不需要缔结什么盟约或条约。\n别忘了，这样的状态已经持续了几千年。

column5: Not that I'm against alliances, or anything like that.\nBut we have no purpose to leave, so I probably won't.\nI need to stay where my role is deemed most important.
column6: 倒不是说我反对结盟之类的。\n只是我们没有离开的理由，所以我也许不会走。\n我得留在最需要我发挥作用的地方。

column5: It's an experience, to say the least.\nHis attention span isn't the best, you know?\nHe'll zone out in the middle of our studies.
column6: 至少可以说，是种“体验”。\n你知道的，他的注意力可不怎么样？\n我们在学习时他会走神。

column5: And he always finds a way to make things humorous.\nIt can be somewhat frustrating when I'm trying to teach him.\nBut maybe that's just me, and I need to loosen up a little.
column6: 而且他总有办法把事情说得搞笑。\n我教他的时候，有时候还真挺让人头疼。\n不过也许只是我太较真，该放松一点。

column5: I knew I wasn't the only one who thought so!\nCompared to him, I can seem a little boring.\nBut that's not true. He's just over the top.
column6: 我就知道不只我这么想！\n跟他一比，我可能显得有点无聊。\n可不是那样。只是他太夸张了。

column5: I've always been pretty mature for my age.\nPerhaps I gained some of his maturity instead.\nAt least he gets along well with the children.
column6: 我一直比同龄人成熟。\n也许我反而从他那儿分到了一些成熟。\n至少他和孩子们相处得很好。

column5: Yeah, yeah, I guess you're right.\nBut we're in positions that are {i}very{/i} sacred.\nIf we don't take this seriously, we'll end up failing.
column6: 是是是，你说得对。\n可我们身处的位置{i}极其{/i}神圣。\n要是我们不认真对待，最终会搞砸。

column5: Maybe I'm just picking up Fortaime's slack.\nI feel like the villagers hold us to a certain \"standard\".\nIf it were just him, he'd fall way short of those standards.
column6: 也许我只是在替福泰姆补漏。\n我感觉村民对我们有某种“标准”。\n要是只有他一个，他远达不到那些标准。

column5: I must sound like an awful person right now.\nI just feel like we all need to act professionally...!
column6: 我现在听起来一定像个很糟的人。\n我只是觉得，我们都该表现得专业些……！

column5: I guess so. We {i}could{/i} hate each other's guts.\nThat would make protecting Valinorth quite hard.\nConsidering that, I think things are pretty good.
column6: 也许吧。我们{i}本可以{/i}互相恨之入骨。\n那样一来，守护瓦利诺斯可就难了。\n这么一想，我觉得现在这样挺好。

column5: I guess I'll just work on my tolerance for his antics.\nI kind of thought you'd agree, and now I feel weird.\nBut if this is just a \"Valessa\" problem, I'll fix it.
column6: 我想我只能提高对他那些闹腾的容忍度了。\n我还以为你会赞同，现在感觉有点怪。\n但如果这只是“瓦莱莎”自己的问题，我会解决。

column5: As always, you have a way of putting things in perspective.\nSorry if it sounded like I was bashing his personality.\nIt was more like an observation, that's all.
column6: 你总有办法帮人看清大局。\n如果我听起来像是在贬低他的性格，抱歉。\n那更像是一种观察，仅此而已。

column5: Yeah, definitely!\nI've been preparing for weeks.\nI's not too complicated, at least for me.
column6: 嗯，当然！\n我已经准备了好几周。\n不算太复杂，至少对我来说。

column5: It might be a little harder for you.\nBut basically, just recite after Mylus.\nAfter that, it's one big celebration.
column6: 对你来说可能会稍微难一点。\n但基本上，只要跟着迈勒斯念就行。\n之后就是一场盛大的庆祝。

column5: My role is minimal, this is your special day.\nAs long as you can handle the spotlight, you're good.\nYou won't have to memorize anything, or make a huge speech.
column6: 我的角色无关紧要，这是属于你的日子。\n只要你能应付得了众人的目光就行。\n你不用背任何东西，也不用发表长篇讲话。

column5: Apparently, Mylus' Father was caught up in other things.\nIt must've been important to shun something like this.\nI wonder if it's related to his disappearance...?
column6: 据说，迈勒斯的父亲当时被别的事缠住了。\n能让他推掉这种事，一定很重要。\n不知道这和他的失踪有没有关系……？

column5: Anyway, that's why it hasn't happened until now.\nIt's supposed to happen when you're much younger.\nBut I don't see any reason why it can't happen now.
column6: 总之，这就是为什么拖到现在才办。\n本来应该在你小得多的时候就举行。\n但我看不出有什么理由说现在不行。

column5: You pledge yourself to Valinorth, and its protection.\nUntil the end of your days, you'll serve our village.\nIn return, you pretty much get to live a life of luxury.
column6: 你宣誓效忠瓦利诺斯，并守护它。\n直到生命尽头，你都将为我们的村庄效力。\n作为回报，你基本上能过上养尊处优的生活。

column5: The benefits are amazing, and a long time coming.\nI hear you'll get a house near Mylus, and loyal servants.\nYou have to be stress-free. Mental strain affects visions.
column6: 待遇非常优厚，而且拖欠已久了。\n我听说你会得到一栋靠近迈勒斯的房子，还有忠诚的仆人。\n你必须保持无忧无虑。精神压力会影响幻象。

column5: Yeah, and I'm actually kind of jealous.\nBut we'll be spending a lot of time together.\nSo I guess I get access to that stuff by association.
column6: 嗯，其实我有点羡慕。\n不过我们会经常待在一起。\n所以我想，我也算沾光能享受到那些东西。

column5: Isn't it a little late to be getting cold feet?\nWe've already been performing these duties forever.\nThis ceremony won't change much. It's just tradition.
column6: 现在打退堂鼓，是不是有点晚了？\n这些职责我们早就一直在履行了。\n这场仪式改变不了什么。不过是传统罢了。

column5: Try not to worry about it too much, alright?\nEverything will be the same tomorrow.\nSame old you. Same old Valinorth.
column6: 尽量别太担心，好吗？\n明天一切都会照旧。\n还是老样子的你。还是老样子的瓦利诺斯。

column5: It might be, but that doesn't mean it's not awesome.\nYou're the most important person in Valinorth, remember?\nYou should be treated with as much respect as possible.
column6: 也许吧，但这不代表它不棒。\n你可是瓦利诺斯最重要的人，记得吗？\n你理应得到尽可能多的尊重。

column5: I'm sure you can turn that stuff down.\nBut it'd be the first time in history that anyone did.\nI think you need to take it, and get rid of your stress.
column6: 我相信你可以拒绝那些东西。\n可那将是历史上头一遭。\n我觉得你该接受，好让自己卸下压力。

column5: As soon as the sun starts to set.\nSo luckily, we still have a few hours.\nPlenty of time to meet with Mylus.
column6: 太阳一开始落山就举行。\n所以还好，我们还有几个小时。\n足够去见迈勒斯了。

column5: This only happens once a generation, so I'm not sure.\nBut I've heard that it goes until the sun starts to rise.\nThat's a bit too much for me. We'll see how long I can last.
column6: 这种事一代人才有一次，所以我也说不准。\n但我听说派对会一直持续到太阳升起。\n对我来说有点吃不消。看看我能撑多久吧。

column5: From what I've seen, you're pretty stressed today.\nI think this ceremony, and the party, will help you unwind.\nAfter it's done, we can take care of whatever we need to.
column6: 据我观察，你今天压力挺大的。\n我想这场仪式和派对能帮你放松。\n等结束之后，我们再处理该处理的事。

column5: This character is not in your party.
column6: 该角色不在你的队伍中。

column5: Only when they lose, do they accuse me of cheating.\nWhere I come from, that's called a sore loser, Airen.
column6: 只有输了，他们才会说我出老千。\n在我老家，这叫输不起，艾琳。

column5: It's only being sore if you're {i}not{/i} cheating.\nPro, are you swindling people in my tavern again...?
column6: 只有在你{i}没{/i}出千的时候，那才叫输不起。\n普洛，你又在我的酒馆里骗人了……？

column5: Now, now, that's such a terrible way of putting it.\nThere's nothing wrong with using sleight of hand to win.\nI like to think that they're paying me for my awesome tricks.
column6: 别急别急，你这么说可太难听了。\n用点手法赢牌没什么不对。\n我更愿意当作，他们是在为我精彩的把戏付钱。

column5: And taking it out on me and my tavern.\nYeah, I can see why you think that's so much fun.\nYou're not the one who has to clean up after the brawls.
column6: 还把账算到我和我的酒馆头上。\n是啊，我明白你为什么会觉得那么好玩。\n毕竟收拾斗殴残局的不是你。

column5: Trust me, I'd kill for a brawl right now.\nAnd remember, this isn't {i}your{/i} tavern...!
column6: 相信我，我现在巴不得大打一场。\n还有，记住，这可不是{i}你的{/i}酒馆……！

column5: Sure it is!\nHas my name on the deed and everything.
column6: 当然是！\n地契上白纸黑字写着我的名字。

column5: Oh yeah? Say that to Damek's face...!\nHe's only keeping you open as an intermediary.\nWe need a neutral place between Mazeo and Valinorth!
column6: 哦，是吗？有本事当着达梅克的面说……！\n他留着你这家店，只是当作中转站。\n马泽奥和瓦利诺斯之间需要一个中立的地方！

column5: Trust me Pro, I'd manage just fine on my own.\nMost people come here for the drinks, and the fun.\nDamek's support is a bonus, not really a necessity.
column6: 相信我，普洛，我自己经营也绰绰有余。\n大多数人是为了喝酒和找乐子才来的。\n达梅克的支持是锦上添花，并非不可或缺。

column5: Besides, how is your investigation going...?\nWeren't you looking into The Seer, or something?\nHard to do that when you play cards all day.
column6: 再说，你的调查进行得怎么样了……？\n你不是在查先知什么的吗？\n整天打牌可查不出什么名堂。

column5: You think I'm playing, but I'm secretly listening.\nYour patrons have given me a great deal of information.
column6: 你以为我在玩牌，其实我在偷听。\n你的客人们可给了我不少情报。

column5: So you're stealing {i}that{/i} from them, too?\nAre you ever gonna give anything back around here?
column6: 所以你连{i}这个{/i}也要从他们那儿偷？\n你什么时候能在这儿回馈点什么？

column5: Yeah, I'm {i}this{/i} close to making my move!\nThere's this really cool sword being held in Valinorth.\nI'm supposed to retrieve it, along with [firstname].
column6: 是啊，我就差{i}这么{/i}一点就要行动了！\n瓦利诺斯藏着一把特别酷的剑。\n我本该和[firstname]一起去把它取回来。

column5: Yeah, I'm {i}this{/i} close to making my move!\nThere's this really cool sword being held in Valinorth.\nI'm supposed to retrieve it, along with [firstname].
column6: 是啊，我就差{i}这么{/i}一点就要行动了！\n瓦利诺斯藏着一把特别酷的剑。\n我本该和[firstname]一起去把它取回来。

column5: Of course, that was almost a week ago.\nDamek is pretty impatient, so I better hurry.\nIf I take any longer, he might send someone else.
column6: 当然，那差不多是一周前的事了。\n达梅克挺没耐心的，我最好抓紧。\n再拖下去，他可能会另派人手。

column5: That's the smartest thing you've said.\nNot today, or this week, just in general.\nIt's not like that blade will come to you.
column6: 这是你说过的最明智的话。\n不是指今天，也不是这周，而是总体上。\n那把剑又不会自己找上门来。

column5: Here, try this new ale that just came in.\nBut after that, you really need to get to work.\nI'm afraid you're scaring away some of my business.
column6: 来，尝尝刚到的这种新麦酒。\n不过喝完这杯，你真得去干活了。\n我担心你快把我的生意吓跑了。

column5: Yeah, yeah, I'll get right on it.\nAt least let me write my boss, first.\nThere's a bunch of stuff he has to know.
column6: 行行行，我马上去办。\n至少先让我给上司写封信。\n有一堆事他得知道。

column5: You mean Damek?\nHe's my boss too, you know.
column6: 你是说达梅克？\n你知道，他也是我的上司。

column5: Yeah, of course!\nI'll grab a paper, and you break out that ale.\nIt better be as good as you're making it sound.
column6: 嗯，当然！\n我拿张纸来，你把那麦酒打开。\n最好有你说的那么好喝。

column5: The Town Square is a serene and beautiful place, like usual.{w}\nA far cry from how I saw it in last night's vision.{w}\nI take a deep breath and relax. We're all safe.
column6: 中央广场一如既往，宁静而美丽。{w}\n和我在昨晚幻象里看到的样子天差地别。{w}\n我深吸一口气，放松下来。我们都安然无恙。

column5: Hey [firstname], nice to see you again!\nI was starting to worry you might be late.\nThankfully, we still have time to spare.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]，很高兴又见到你！\n我刚才还担心你会迟到呢。\n还好，我们还有富余时间。

column5: She runs up to me and gives me a tight hug.{w}\nI glance over at Fortaime, and he appears embarrassed.
column6: 她跑过来，紧紧抱住我。{w}\n我瞥了一眼福泰姆，他显得有些尴尬。

column5: Oh my, is this a hint of romance I see?\nAnd in public too? People will start to talk!
column6: 哎呀，我看到的这是爱情的火花吗？\n还是在众目睽睽之下？大家可要说闲话了！

column5: Shut it, Fortaime! Nobody asked you!\nI was just excited to see [firstname].\nRemember how special today is...?
column6: 闭嘴，福泰姆！没人问你！\n我只是见到[firstname]太高兴了。\n记得今天有多特别吗……？

column5: Shut it, Fortaime! Nobody asked you!\nI was just excited to see [firstname].\nRemember how special today is...?
column6: 闭嘴，福泰姆！没人问你！\n我只是见到[firstname]太高兴了。\n记得今天有多特别吗……？

column5: Oh my. A lovers quarrel, too?\nGuess today is special for me after all.
column6: 哎呀。还吵起小两口架了？\n看来今天对我来说也够特别的。

column5: Hey, I'm happy for you too!\nI was gonna hug you, I swear.
column6: 嘿，我也为你高兴！\n我本来也要抱你的，我发誓。

column5: Whoa, I was just joking around.\nIf you're serious, then I'm kind of jealous.
column6: 哇，我只是开个玩笑。\n你要当真的话，那我还有点羡慕。

column5: That's pretty much confirmation in my books!\nDon't worry, your secret is safe with me.
column6: 在我看来，这基本算是坐实了！\n放心，你的秘密我会守住的。

column5: But I guess there's more important matters at hand.\nSorry for getting sidetracked, I'm all over the place.\nDo your thing. I'll be waiting over there by the tank.
column6: 不过我想眼下有更重要的事。\n抱歉跑题了，我老是这样没个正形。\n你们聊吧。我在那边水塔旁等你们。

column5: He runs off to the water tank, and rests against it.{w}\nHe's definitely out of earshot, so I could talk to Valessa.{w}\nWe need to meet up with Mylus, so they could hear about my vision.
column6: 他跑到水塔旁，靠了上去。{w}\n他肯定听不见了，我可以和瓦莱莎说话。{w}\n我们得去见迈勒斯，好让他们听听我的幻象。

column5: I swear, Fortaime can be so insufferable.\nBe glad you don't work with him as much as I do.\nHe keeps things {i}interesting{/i}, to say the least.
column6: 我发誓，福泰姆有时候真让人受不了。\n还好你不用像我这样天天跟他共事。\n至少可以说，他总能让人{i}不得清静{/i}。

column5: Just don't say that to his face or anything.\nIt's tolerable, but I wish he'd grow up already.\nAnyway, something doesn't add up to me here.
column6: 只是别当着他的面说这些就是了。\n还忍得了，但我希望他能成熟点。\n总之，这里有件事我怎么想都不对劲。

column5: Hey, I'm just joking around!\nWe're best friends, we're supposed to poke fun.\nEither way, something about this doesn't add up to me.
column6: 嘿，我只是开开玩笑！\n我们是最好的朋友，本来就该互相打趣。\n不管怎样，这件事我怎么想都不对劲。

column5: You mean... you and Fortaime...!?\nTrust me, that's the last thing I expected to hear.\nJust one of the many things that don't add up today.
column6: 你是说……你和福泰姆……！？\n相信我，这是我最没想到会听到的话。\n今天不对劲的事，这只是其中之一。

column5: Of course we can, we're best friends!\nI was just poking fun, aren't we supposed to do that?\nJeeze, something about this doesn't add up at all.
column6: 我们当然能，我们是最好的朋友！\n我只是在开玩笑，我们不就该这样吗？\n天哪，这件事怎么想都不对劲。

column5: Fortaime would never willingly walk away from us.\nHe'd only do that if he's not allowed to listen in.\nSo correct me if I'm wrong, but you had a vision, didn't you?
column6: 福泰姆绝不会主动从我们身边走开。\n他只有不被允许旁听时才会那样。\n所以如果我说错了就纠正我——你看到幻象了，对吧？

column5: Oh, really...?\nI knew something was off. You seem different.\nI didn't want to bring it up, but now I know why.
column6: 哦，真的……？\n我就知道有什么不对劲。你看起来不一样了。\n我本来不想提，但现在我知道为什么了。

column5: Should we go to The Grand Tree, then?\nIt might be good to discuss this in private.\nIf I tell the villagers, they won't bother us.
column6: 那我们该去巨树那儿吗？\n私下讨论这件事或许更好。\n我跟村民们说一声，他们就不会来打扰我们。

column5: Whoa, you're starting to creep me out [firstname].\nInvolving The Elder? That's very... serious.
column6: 哇，你开始让我有点发毛了，[firstname]。\n要牵扯到长老？那可就……非常严重了。

column5: Whoa, you're starting to creep me out [firstname].\nInvolving The Elder? That's very... serious.
column6: 哇，你开始让我有点发毛了，[firstname]。\n要牵扯到长老？那可就……非常严重了。

column5: But I trust your judgment, I really do.\nLet's grab Fortaime and head to Mylus' place.\nIf it's actually that bad, he should be there with us.
column6: 但我相信你的判断，真的。\n我们叫上福泰姆，去迈勒斯那儿。\n要是真有那么严重，他该和我们在一起。

column5: Just promise me one thing. Do your best to keep calm.\nSome of the villagers are already looking your way.\nIf they see you freaking out, they'll freak out too.
column6: 答应我一件事。尽量保持镇定。\n有些村民已经在朝我们这边看了。\n要是他们看到你惊慌失措，他们也会跟着慌。

column5: Try not to waste too much time here, [firstname].\nI'm dressed in layers, and this humidity is gross.\nWouldn't want to ruin my outfit before your ceremony.
column6: 尽量别在这儿耽搁太久，[firstname]。\n我穿了好几层，这潮气太难受了。\n可不想在你的仪式前把衣服弄坏。

column5: Try not to waste too much time here, [firstname].\nI'm dressed in layers, and this humidity is gross.\nWouldn't want to ruin my outfit before your ceremony.
column6: 尽量别在这儿耽搁太久，[firstname]。\n我穿了好几层，这潮气太难受了。\n可不想在你的仪式前把衣服弄坏。

column5: Hey, I guess you didn't get to do your water run.\nYou should do it as soon as you get a chance!\nI finished mine up just before you got here.
column6: 嘿，我猜你还没去取水吧。\n一有机会就赶紧去！\n你到这儿之前我刚取完我的那份。

column5: So, this might be the last time we see the town square.\nIs there anything we should do before we go...?
column6: 那么，这也许是我们最后一次看这个广场了。\n走之前有什么该做的事吗……？

column5: I guess one last drink would be nice.\nThe water from Valinorth is always so pure.\nWant to share some with me, Valessa?
column6: 我想最后喝一杯也不错。\n瓦利诺斯的水总是那么清甜。\n要不要和我一起喝点，瓦莱莎？

column5: Sure, we can use the cups I left here earlier.\nI was just finishing my water run when we all met up.
column6: 好啊，可以用我先前留在这儿的杯子。\n我们碰头的时候，我刚取完水。

column5: So what should we toast to?
column6: 那我们该为什么干杯呢？

column5: Toast...?
column6: 干杯……？

column5: Yeah, this is a big day, right?\nWe should probably drink to {i}something{/i}.\nEspecially if it's the last time we might be here.
column6: 是啊，今天可是个大日子，对吧？\n我们总得为{i}点什么{/i}喝一杯。\n尤其是这可能还是我们最后一次来这儿。

column5: Oh, let's see...
column6: 哦，让我想想……

column5: What about \"new beginnings\"?\nOr something like \"being with friends\"?
column6: 就说“新的开始”怎么样？\n或者“与朋友相伴”之类的？

column5: What about \"new beginnings {i}with{/i} friends\"?\nI think that's rather fitting for us.
column6: 那“与朋友{i}一起{/i}开启新的开始”如何？\n我觉得这对我们挺贴切的。

column5: Sounds good to me.\nTo new beginnings with friends.\nMay our bonds never break.
column6: 我觉得不错。\n为与朋友一起开启新的开始。\n愿我们的羁绊永不破裂。

column5: Water often spills out, and gets the ground wet.{w}\nIt's mushy, and soft to the touch. Gross.
column6: 水经常溢出来，把地面弄湿。{w}\n踩上去又软又黏。真恶心。

column5: Whoa, your shoes are so messy...!\nAnd just before your big ceremony!\nBack away and watch your step!
column6: 哇，你的鞋弄得这么脏……！\n偏偏就在你盛大的仪式之前！\n往后站站，小心脚下！

column5: Cannot access content at this time.\nIf there is an X, you must complete preceding Heart-to-Hearts.\nIf there is a checkmark, you must move on to the next Heart-to-Heart.
column6: 此时无法访问内容。\n如果显示 X，你需要先完成前置的“心与心”剧情。\n如果显示对勾，你需要继续推进到下一个“心与心”。

column5: Whoa, that's disgusting...!\nThose things could be so dirty, you know.\nAt least wait until there's no one around.
column6: 哇，真恶心……！\n你知道，那些东西可能特别脏。\n至少等没人的时候再去碰。

column5: I saw you staring down that faucet...\nTrust me, I've been tempted more than once.\nBut the villagers need a better example.
column6: 我看见你盯着那个水龙头了……\n相信我，我不止一次也心动过。\n但村民们需要一个更好的榜样。

column5: The ground here is paved, and dry.{w}\nIt's not wet like the rest of the soil.{w}\nThis would be the best place for me to stand.
column6: 这里的地面铺了石板，是干的。{w}\n不像其他地方的泥土那样潮湿。{w}\n这里最适合我站。

column5: It appears to be written by Mylus' Father, the previous Elder.
column6: 看起来是迈勒斯的父亲，也就是上一任长老写的。

column5: There's a book sitting here, it's wet and stained.{w}\nMost likely water damage, due to its proximity to the tank.{w}\nWhen I approach it, Fortaime laughs and apologizes to me.
column6: 这里放着一本书，又湿又脏。{w}\n多半是因为离水塔太近，被水泡坏了。{w}\n我走近时，福泰姆笑着向我道歉。

column5: Sorry, I think I dropped that when I was waiting!\nIt's something I picked up from Mylus' house a few days ago.\nYou're free to take it, I have no use for it anymore.
column6: 抱歉，我想是我在这儿等的时候掉的！\n这是我几天前从迈勒斯家拿的。\n你尽管拿去，我用不上了。

column5: Damek and Ulric gathered in the town square come morning.{w}\nThe road to Valinorth would be long and fraught with danger.{w}\nBut this time, Damek was certain he'd sent the right man.
column6: 清晨，达梅克和乌尔里克在中央广场碰面。{w}\n前往瓦利诺斯的路漫长且危机四伏。{w}\n但这一次，达梅克确信自己派对了人。

column5: Are you sure you'll be okay on your own?\nIt's not too late to ask for some escorts.
column6: 你确定一个人没问题吗？\n现在要几个护卫还不算晚。

column5: Yes, Damek. Stop asking.\nI'll be fine, and I'm well aware of the dangers.\nBringing more people would just put them in harm's way.
column6: 是的，达梅克。别问了。\n我没事，危险我很清楚。\n多带人只会让他们也身处险境。

column5: Well, forgive me for caring!\nI just wanted to make sure you're comfortable.\nIf the attack is imminent, you'll have to rush.
column6: 哎，关心你也有错！\n我只是想确保你安排妥当。\n要是进攻迫在眉睫，你就得加快脚步。

column5: I expect it'll take me under a day.\nI'll arrive in the dead of night, or maybe early morning.\nSeeking out [firstname] will be the first thing I do.
column6: 我估计用不了一天。\n我会在深夜，或者清早到达。\n第一件事就是去找[firstname]。

column5: I expect it'll take me under a day.\nI'll arrive in the dead of night, or maybe early morning.\nSeeking out [firstname] will be the first thing I do.
column6: 我估计用不了一天。\n我会在深夜，或者清早到达。\n第一件事就是去找[firstname]。

column5: Fantastic, then things will go perfectly.\nMake sure to give the rest of the town a heads up.\nYou can all evacuate together. You'll blend right in.
column6: 太好了，那一切都会顺利。\n记得提前通知镇上的其他人。\n你们可以一起撤离。你会混在其中不显眼。

column5: But remember, you need to stop by Mylus' and grab the blade.\nOtherwise, The Triumvirate will seize it when they attack.\nIf I'm honest, I don't think we stand a chance without it.
column6: 但记住，你得顺路去迈勒斯那儿取剑。\n否则三人执政团进攻时会把剑夺走。\n说实话，没有那把剑，我觉得我们毫无胜算。

column5: I can't believe they're attacking Valinorth.\nThe occupation of Mazeo is still so fresh.\nThankfully, they haven't found us yet.
column6: 真不敢相信他们要进攻瓦利诺斯。\n马泽奥被占领的事还历历在目。\n还好他们还没找到我们。

column5: Right under their noses, just as we should be.\nI'm going to meet with the Mayor after this, actually.\nI'll see about fully claiming those underground tunnels.
column6: 就在他们眼皮底下，这正是我们该待的位置。\n其实这之后我就要去见市长。\n我会去谈谈把那片地下隧道彻底弄到手的事。

column5: Whatever they were digging for, they've stopped.\nI think it would make a fine base of operations.\nGetting the deed shouldn't be too difficult.
column6: 不管他们当初在挖什么，都已经停了。\n我觉得那里很适合当行动基地。\n拿到地契应该不太难。

column5: Wait, you mean we'll have a new home?\nNo more sleeping on the hard tavern floor?
column6: 等等，你是说我们要有新家了？\n不用再睡酒馆那硬邦邦的地板了？

column5: Never again. It's time we get established.\nI have some large shoes to fill as The General.\nThe first step is finding us a fitting home.
column6: 再也不用。是时候站稳脚跟了。\n身为将军，我有很多要担起的责任。\n第一步就是给我们找个像样的家。

column5: Good, I'm glad to hear it.\nBut one last thing before I go.\nIs it true what I've heard about Mylus...?
column6: 很好，很高兴听你这么说。\n不过走之前还有最后一件事。\n我听到的那些关于迈勒斯的传闻，是真的吗……？

column5: Absolutely, so please be kind to him.\nHe'll be a valuable ally in the coming days.\nBest of luck on your vacation, Ulric.
column6: 千真万确，所以请对他客气点。\n接下来的日子里，他会是个宝贵的盟友。\n祝你“度假”顺利，乌尔里克。

column5: Trust me, I wish that's what it was.\nBut I'll try retrieving [firstname] and the blade as soon as possible.\nGood luck with the Mayor. I think you'll need it.
column6: 相信我，我倒希望真是度假。\n但我会尽快接回[firstname]和那把剑。\n祝你跟市长谈得顺利。我想你会需要的。

column5: Trust me, I wish that's what it was.\nBut I'll try retrieving [firstname] and the blade as soon as possible.\nGood luck with the Mayor. I think you'll need it.
column6: 相信我，我倒希望真是度假。\n但我会尽快接回[firstname]和那把剑。\n祝你跟市长谈得顺利。我想你会需要的。

column5: But coming back to a home, with an actual battle plan?\nIt's starting to feel like our cause has some real weight to it.\nI feel bad for doubting you Damek. You're doing a great job.
column6: 可带着真正的作战计划回到一个家？\n我开始觉得我们的事业有分量了。\n我为自己怀疑过你而愧疚，达梅克。你做得很好。

column5: Sovy, what is the meaning of this intrusion?
column6: 索维，你这样闯入是什么意思？

column5: Halin has finished his interrogation, Masters.\nI thought it would be wise to relay the results.\nUnless you were plotting behind our backs...?
column6: 师父们，哈林已经审问完毕。\n我想把结果转达给你们才是明智之举。\n除非……你们一直在背地里谋划什么？

column5: We would never do such a thing.\nInformation is granted to you as we see fit.\nIf you are left in the dark, it is not permanent.
column6: 我们绝不会做那种事。\n情报何时给你们，由我们决定。\n就算你们暂时不知情，也不会是永久的。

column5: But please, tell us what Halin discovered.\nWe have a feeling our theories are similar.
column6: 不过，请告诉我们哈林发现了什么。\n我们有种感觉，我们的推测是相似的。

column5: Yes, of course.\nThe Exodus Wielder {i}is{/i} located in Valinorth.\nI am ready to launch our attack at a moment's notice.
column6: 是的，当然。\n流亡之刃的持剑人{i}确实{/i}在瓦利诺斯。\n我随时准备发动进攻。

column5: Good. Then it is time you hear the rest.\nValinorth is just a small part of our larger plan.\nWe see no more reason to withold this information.
column6: 很好。那么是时候让你听听其余的部分了。\n瓦利诺斯只是我们更大计划中的一小部分。\n我们再没有理由隐瞒这些情报了。

column5: That much was obvious, Masters.\nWhy did you keep it from me for so long?\nHalin and I are more than loyal enough...!
column6: 这点显而易见，师父们。\n你们为什么瞒了我这么久？\n我和哈林已经足够忠诚了……！

column5: Sovy, this is not a matter of loyalty.\nWe are sure you'll understand when you hear.\nIt would not be wise to doubt our word.
column6: 索维，这无关忠诚。\n我们相信，你听了之后就会明白。\n怀疑我们的话，可不是明智之举。

column5: Yes, yes. My apologies.\nNobody likes being left in the dark.\nI will ensure my words sound less doubtful.
column6: 是，是。我道歉。\n没人喜欢被蒙在鼓里。\n我会注意，别让我的话听起来那么充满怀疑。

column5: If there is a greater plan at play, I am honored.\nI find no greater pleasure than serving your cause.\nSo please, tell me what you wish, and it will happen.
column6: 如果背后还有更大的计划，我深感荣幸。\n为你们的事业效力，是我最大的快乐。\n所以请告诉我你们的意愿，我一定会办到。

column5: We've led you to believe that Valinorth is our goal.\nHowever, it is just the beginning of a much larger plan.
column6: 我们一直让你以为瓦利诺斯就是我们的目标。\n然而，那只是一个更宏大计划的开端。

column5: Today, you will learn the {i}true{/i} nature of the spirit realm.
column6: 今天，你将了解到灵界{i}真正{/i}的本质。

column5: I look at the water tank, thinking of the vision that started this all.{w}\nBack then, I thought we could use the water to fight the flames.{w}\nLittle did I know, that entire vision was just a trick to bait us.
column6: 我看着水塔，想起这一切起始的那个幻象。{w}\n当时我以为我们可以用水来扑灭火焰。{w}\n却不知那整个幻象不过是引我们上钩的诡计。

column5: However, that was the first time I ever laid eyes on Sovy.{w}\nI'll never forget what he did to me. He killed me without hesitation.{w}\nBut is he different now? Or was he ever really like that to begin with...?
column6: 不过，那是我第一次见到索维。{w}\n我永远不会忘记他对我做的事。他毫不犹豫地杀了我。{w}\n可他现在变了吗？还是说他本来就不是那样的人……？

column5: So, this is Valinorth. I've heard stories, but never been.\nWell — unless you count that vision The Triumvirate tricked you with.\nI must apologize for that. I knew what was going on, and I played along.
column6: 那么，这就是瓦利诺斯。我听过不少传闻，却从未来过。\n嗯——除非把三人执政团骗你看到的那个幻象也算上。\n为此我必须道歉。我知道当时是怎么回事，却还是配合了。

column5: It's not like I could've done anything else. Valinorth was too far away.\nThat, and they still had me under their thrall. I was theirs to command.\nAt least I was able to break free. I feel bad for Halin, I truly do.
column6: 我当时也做不了别的。瓦利诺斯太远了。\n何况他们仍控制着我。我任由他们驱使。\n至少我总算挣脱了。我真为哈林感到难过，真的。

column5: He looks around the town square.{w}\nIt looks like he's enamored by Valinorth.{w}\nAlmost as if he's looking at a wonder of the world.
column6: 他环顾中央广场。{w}\n看起来他迷上了瓦利诺斯。{w}\n仿佛在观赏世界奇观。

column5: I need to ask — what did you think of me...?\nThe moment we met in that vision. Who was I to you?\nA mindless slave? A killer? Or perhaps a man who was lost?
column6: 我得问一句——你当时怎么看我……？\n我们在那个幻象里相遇的那一刻。我对你来说是谁？\n一个没有思想的奴隶？一个杀手？还是……一个迷失的人？

column5: I guess I was. Oh well, it was worth a shot.\nI commited atrocities in their name. I feel irredeemable. \nThe fact that your'e giving me a chance? That's a {i}true{/i} miracle.
column6: 我想我是吧。算了，问一下也无妨。\n我以他们的名义犯下过暴行。我觉得自己无可救药。\n你竟然愿意给我一个机会？那真是{i}不折不扣{/i}的奇迹。

column5: All I ever wanted was to ensure that Alestia's true rulers remained in power.\nLittle did I know, The Triumvirate was lying to me all along. {i}You{/i} are the true ruler.\nNow I know why they wanted to kill you so bad. You're a massive threat. Plain and simple.
column6: 我一直只想确保阿莱斯蒂亚真正的统治者掌权。\n却不知三人执政团从头到尾都在骗我。{i}你{/i}才是真正的统治者。\n现在我知道他们为什么那么想杀你了。你是巨大的威胁。就这么简单。

column5: Excuse me...? Please, don't make jokes like that.\nI'm being serious here, [firstname]. You should be serious, too.\nI really hope the weight of our cause doesn't rest on someone so childish.
column6: 什么……？拜托，别开那种玩笑。\n我是认真的，[firstname]。你也该认真点。\n我真希望我们事业的重量，不是压在一个这么幼稚的人身上。

column5: I guess you're right. But The Triumvirate made that vision.\nI know they did it to trick you — but I was still a part of it.\nHow they portrayed me would be how they {i}saw{/i} me.
column6: 你说得也许对。可那个幻象是三人执政团造出来的。\n我知道他们是为了骗你——可我还是参与了其中。\n他们把我塑造成什么样，就说明他们{i}看{/i}我是什么样。

column5: He shakes his head, and looks around the town some more.{w}\nHis eyes become fixated on the post office, and he smiles slightly.
column6: 他摇摇头，又打量了镇子一会儿。{w}\n他的目光定格在邮局上，微微笑了。

column5: A post office...? I haven't seen one of those in ages.\nI couldn't travel much when I was younger, so I collected stamps.\nThe drawings of places around Alestia — that was the closest I ever got.
column6: 邮局……？我好久没见过邮局了。\n我年轻时没法到处走，所以就集邮。\n那些印着阿莱斯蒂亚各地风景的图案——是我离那些地方最近的一次。

column5: He walks toward it, so I make sure to follow him.{w}\nThis is the first time he's ever mentioned anything about his past.{w}\nIt's hard to imagine that he was anything other than The Grand Inquisitor.
column6: 他朝那儿走去，我也跟了上去。{w}\n这是他第一次提起自己的过去。{w}\n很难想象他除了大审判官之外还有别的样子。

column5: But the art never really matches up with the place when you see it in person.\nI remember collecting the Balteus set, and being shocked when I actually got there.\nIt's not really a good or a bad difference. It's just interesting to see how they compare.
column6: 但等你亲眼见到那些地方，图案其实跟实地并不一样。\n我记得收集巴尔泰乌斯那套邮票时，真正到了那里，我大吃一惊。\n这算不上好或坏的差别。只是把两者对照看看，挺有意思。

column5: That's not really something I'd like to talk about right now.\nDo you mind if I go inside and buy some really quick?\nIt won't take too long, I promise. Just wait for me.
column6: 这事我现在不太想谈。\n介意我进去快速买一些吗？\n我保证不会太久。等等我。

column5: Oh, wonderful. Then you won't mind if I go buy some...?\nI shouldn't be too long. It's just for old time's sake, you know?\nJust wait for me. We can get back on track as soon as I return.
column6: 哦，太好了。那你不介意我进去买一些吧……？\n应该不会太久。你知道，就是怀旧一下。\n等等我。我一回来我们就继续正事。

column5: I nod, and he smiles at me.{w}\nHe runs into the post office and buys some stamps.{w}\nA look of childlike glee is worn on his face when he returns.
column6: 我点点头，他冲我笑了笑。{w}\n他跑进邮局，买了一些邮票。{w}\n他回来时，脸上带着孩子般的喜悦。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nYou know what it's like — sometimes you just need to do something.\nThis is the first time I've truly been free, so I almost couldn't resist.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n你懂的——有时候你就是想做点什么。\n这是我第一次真正自由，所以我几乎按捺不住。

column5: I'll save these, and perhaps we can write each other after the war.\nYou'll be incredibly busy, so I can't expect to earn a lot of your time.
column6: 我会把这些收好，也许战后我们可以互相写信。\n你会忙得不可开交，所以我也不敢奢望能占用你多少时间。

column5: Perfect. We'll figure something out when the time comes.\nFor now, I think we have to focus on more important things.
column6: 好极了。到时候我们再想办法。\n眼下，我想我们得专注于更重要的事。

column5: I'm not sure how to respond to that, so I won't.\nLet's focus on more important things for now.
column6: 我不知道该怎么回应那句话，那就不回应了。\n先专注于更重要的事吧。

column5: Very well. I suppose I'll survive either way.\nLet's focus on more important things for now, then.
column6: 好吧。我想不管怎样我都活得下去。\n那我们就先专注于更重要的事吧。

column5: Well, I wouldn't go that far — but suit yourself.\nIn that case, let's focus on something more important.
column6: 嗯，我倒不会说得那么夸张——随你吧。\n既然如此，我们就专注于更重要的事。

column5: He looks at the blade on my back, and assumes a thinking pose.
column6: 他看着我背上的剑，摆出思索的姿势。

column5: You could use some training, couldn't you?\nAnything to give you an edge in the upcoming battle.\nI have years of practice, so I can teach you almost everything.
column6: 你需要练练，对吧？\n任何能在接下来的战斗中占上风的东西。\n我练了多年，几乎什么都能教你。

column5: We shouldn't stay here too long, though. Schedules and all that.\nIf we start training while we travel, it'll be more efficient in the end.\nWe can't waste too much time before setting sail for Balteus.
column6: 不过我们不该在这儿待太久。行程什么的。\n如果我们在旅途中开始训练，最终效率会更高。\n启航前往巴尔泰乌斯之前，不能浪费太多时间。

column5: I nod. It's true — he could teach me a lot about this blade.{w}\nI feel like I'd be needing that knowledge in the coming days.{w}\nPerhaps having him join us wasn't a bad idea after all.
column6: 我点点头。的确——关于这把剑，他能教我很多。{w}\n我感觉接下来的日子里，我会需要这些知识。{w}\n也许让他加入我们，终究不是个坏主意。

column5: Wonderful. Normally, I'd call you an Apprentice at this point.\nBut I'm past that. I need to drop the behavior that The Triumvirate taught me.\nSo — you're not an Apprentice to me — you're a friend; and I'll help you.
column6: 太好了。换作以前，这时候我会称你为学徒。\n但我已经不再那样了。我得丢掉三人执政团教给我的那套做派。\n所以——对我来说你不是学徒——你是朋友；而我会帮你。

column5: We start walking away from the town square, and he inspects his stamps.{w}\nIt was crazy how different he seems from how he was before. I'm taken aback.{w}\nBut if this was the new him, and not some sort of facade — he'd be welcomed.
column6: 我们开始离开中央广场，他端详着那些邮票。{w}\n他和从前简直判若两人，这太不可思议了。我不禁愣住。{w}\n但如果这就是新的他，而非某种伪装——那他值得被接纳。

column5: The Grand Tree towers above everything else in Valinorth.{w}\nAnd because of Valinorth's altitude, it towers above the world.{w}\nWe take slow steps across the makeshift bridge, holding onto the sides.
column6: 巨树高耸于瓦利诺斯的一切之上。{w}\n而由于瓦利诺斯本身的海拔，它仿佛高耸于整个世界之上。{w}\n我们扶着两侧，缓缓走过那座临时搭建的桥。

column5: Valessa stops in her tracks, taking in the surroundings.{w}\nA hint of confusion appears on her face as she breaks the silence.{w}\nStopping as well, Fortaime and I listen to her words.
column6: 瓦莱莎停下脚步，环顾四周。{w}\n她打破沉默时，脸上浮现出一丝困惑。{w}\n我和福泰姆也停下来，听她说话。

column5: Alright, we really need to talk.\n[firstname]. What are you thoughts on all of this?\nYou've been totally silent since we left Mylus'.
column6: 好了，我们真的得谈谈。\n[firstname]。你对这一切怎么看？\n自从离开迈勒斯那儿，你就一句话都没说。

column5: Alright, we really need to talk.\n[firstname]. What are you thoughts on all of this?\nYou've been totally silent since we left Mylus'.
column6: 好了，我们真的得谈谈。\n[firstname]。你对这一切怎么看？\n自从离开迈勒斯那儿，你就一句话都没说。

column5: Hey Valessa, no prying.\nLet him open up when he wants to.
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎，别追问了。\n等他想说的时候自然会开口。

column5: Hey Valessa, no prying.\nLet her open up when she wants to.
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎，别追问了。\n等她想说的时候自然会开口。

column5: I'm just curious, that's all.\nIt's not like Mylus treated us to afternoon tea.\nEverything is different. Besides, venting can help.
column6: 我只是好奇，仅此而已。\n迈勒斯又不是请我们喝了顿下午茶。\n一切都变了。再说，把心事说出来会有帮助。

column5: Oh, okay.\nJust thought I'd give you the opportunity.\nIt's always nice to have friends with open ears.
column6: 哦，好吧。\n我只是想给你个机会。\n有愿意倾听的朋友总是好事。

column5: Yeah, I feel exactly the same.\nIn just a couple hours, everything changed.\nThey can't expect us to adapt {i}that{/i} quickly.
column6: 嗯，我完全有同感。\n短短几个小时，一切都变了。\n他们不能指望我们{i}那么{/i}快就适应。

column5: You've always had purpose, actually.\nBut I think I understand what you mean.\nYou aren't just another Seer, you're special.
column6: 其实你一直都有信念。\n但我想我明白你的意思。\n你不是普通意义上的先知，你很特别。

column5: You've always had purpose, actually.\nBut I think I understand what you mean.\nYou aren't just another Seeress, you're special.
column6: 其实你一直都有目标。\n但我想我明白你的意思。\n你不是普通意义上的先知，你很特别。

column5: There's not much else we {i}can{/i} do.\nI'm sure that Damek will have a lot to teach us.\nMaybe when we get there, we won't feel so lost.
column6: 我们{i}能{/i}做的也不多。\n我相信达梅克有很多东西要教我们。\n也许到了那儿，我们就不会这么迷茫了。

column5: She turns back around, and we continue walking.{w}\nI try to admire the scenery, but that attempt is short lived.{w}\nFortaime, who had taken the lead, also stops in his tracks.
column6: 她转过身，我们继续往前走。{w}\n我试着欣赏风景，但没持续多久。{w}\n走在最前面的福泰姆也停下了脚步。

column5: Actually, on the subject of venting...\nThere's something I need to get off my chest.\nOr, I guess, there's something I need to ask you two.
column6: 其实，说到把心事说出来……\n有件事我一直憋在心里。\n或者说，有件事我想问问你们俩。

column5: Sure, what is it?
column6: 好啊，什么事？

column5: I know we don't like talking about this.\nAnd sometimes, we pretend it never even happened.\nBut we can't anymore. We're going to Mazeo.
column6: 我知道我们不愿谈这个。\n有时候，我们假装它从没发生过。\n但不能再这样了。我们要去马泽奥。

column5: So I think now we need to face the facts.\nThat's the last place our parents were—\nI mean, they were there when it happened.
column6: 所以我觉得，现在我们必须面对现实。\n那是我们父母最后待过的地方——\n我是说，事情发生的时候，他们就在那儿。

column5: Casualties of the occupation...
column6: 占领的牺牲者……

column5: Now we have the chance to fight back against The Triumvirate.\nThey were directly responsible for what happened there.\nAre we doing this for Alestia, or for ourselves...?
column6: 现在我们有机会反击三人执政团了。\n他们对那里发生的事负有直接责任。\n我们这么做是为了阿莱斯蒂亚，还是为了我们自己……？

column5: You mean revenge...?\nFortaime, I don't know how to answer that.\nAll of our parents. That was so long ago.
column6: 你是说复仇……？\n福泰姆，我不知道该怎么回答。\n我们所有的父母。那是好久以前的事了。

column5: I don't know if that makes me a bad person or not.\nBut we can't just fight because Mylus told us to.\nWe each need a purpose, even if they're different.
column6: 我不知道这样想是不是说明我是个坏人。\n但我们不能只因为迈勒斯叫我们打就上战场。\n我们每个人都需要一个信念，哪怕各不相同。

column5: I guess I want Alestia's freedom.\nIs that not reason enough to fight?
column6: 我想我想要阿莱斯蒂亚的自由。\n这还不够作为战斗的理由吗？

column5: That's a goal, Valessa. Not a purpose.\nLet me ask [firstname]. Why do {i}you{/i} fight...?\nWhat weight will you carry with that blade?
column6: 那是个目标，瓦莱莎。不是信念。\n让我问问[firstname]。你{i}为什么{/i}而战……？\n拿着那把剑，你将背负什么？

column5: That's a goal, Valessa. Not a purpose.\nLet me ask [firstname]. Why do {i}you{/i} fight...?\nWhat weight will you carry with that blade?
column6: 那是个目标，瓦莱莎。不是信念。\n让我问问[firstname]。你{i}为什么{/i}而战……？\n拿着那把剑，你将背负什么？

column5: Good. So I'm not the only one, then.\nI didn't fully realize it until we left Mylus' house.\nThis is our chance to fight back. To take them down.
column6: 好。看来不只我一个这么想。\n直到离开迈勒斯家，我才真正意识到这一点。\n这是我们反击的机会。扳倒他们。

column5: That's a great purpose, [firstname].\nWith better rulers, people won't suffer anymore.\nEvery time you swing that blade, remember your answer.
column6: 那是个了不起的信念，[firstname]。\n有了更好的统治者，人们就不会再受苦。\n每次挥剑，都记住你的答案。

column5: That's a great purpose, [firstname].\nWith better rulers, people won't suffer anymore.\nEvery time you swing that blade, remember your answer.
column6: 那是个了不起的信念，[firstname]。\n有了更好的统治者，人们就不会再受苦。\n每次挥剑，都记住你的答案。

column5: Good. Tap into that drive whenever you can.\nDon't let any swing of your blade lack purpose.\nA fight without purpose is a fight you'll never win.
column6: 好。只要有机会，就调动那份动力。\n别让你挥出的任何一剑缺乏信念。\n没有信念的战斗，你永远赢不了。

column5: Forced...?\nThat's not true. You have a purpose, I know it.\nOtherwise, we wouldn't be here getting this blade.
column6: 被逼……？\n不是那样的。你有信念，我知道。\n否则，我们也不会来这儿取这把剑。

column5: Alright, alright, I'll back off.\nSorry if it was a touchy subject or something.\nI just think everything is better if you have a reason.
column6: 好了好了，我不问了。\n如果戳到了什么痛处，抱歉。\n我只是觉得，人有个理由，一切都会更好。

column5: I have more to say though, so hold on.\nOur parents went to Mazeo together, as a group of friends.\nNow we're doing the same. And trust me, I'm worried.
column6: 不过我还有话要说，等等。\n我们的父母当年是一群朋友，一起去了马泽奥。\n现在我们也在做同样的事。相信我，我很担心。

column5: They got caught up in a fight, and we will too.\nBut I don't want to die. I want to save Alestia...\nSo promise me we'll stay together, right until the end.
column6: 他们卷进了一场战斗，我们也会。\n但我不想死。我想拯救阿莱斯蒂亚……\n所以答应我，我们会一直在一起，直到最后。

column5: There we go, that's the spirit!\nWith that attitude, we'll never lose.\nNow let's get that blade, and head to Mazeo.
column6: 这就对了，这才像话！\n有这种心态，我们绝不会输。\n现在去取那把剑，然后出发去马泽奥。
